format.purpose: Pins the expected statement split of a module artifact for every implementation of the splitter. The canonical Python splitter lives in src/preproc/module/artifact.py; the in-database Lua splitter lives in sql/lua/module_install.lua. Both MUST reproduce every case here exactly, and MUST reject every error_case.
format.value_encoding: A `text`, and each entry of `statements`, is EITHER a JSON string taken literally, OR a JSON array of parts. A part is either a literal string or an object {"repeat_unit": <string>, "count": <integer>} which materializes to repeat_unit repeated count times. Materialize an array by concatenating its parts in order. The array form exists only so the chunk-boundary case can pin a 2,000,000-character artifact without storing a 2 MB blob.
grammar: Line endings are normalized to LF before splitting: CRLF and a bare CR both become LF.

A marker line is a COMPLETE physical line whose content, ignoring surrounding whitespace, is exactly `--/` (block open) or exactly `/` (block close). `SELECT 1; --/` is therefore not a marker; it is a statement followed by a comment.

A `--/` line opens a block. Every following line up to the next lone `/` line is the statement body, preserved VERBATIM: the body is never scanned for terminators, comments, or quotes, so a statement whose own syntax needs a trailing `;` (CREATE FUNCTION ... END;) survives intact. Neither marker line appears in the yielded statement.

Outside a block, a statement is terminated by the first `;` that falls outside a single-quoted string literal, a double-quoted identifier, a `--` line comment, and a `/* */` block comment. The terminating `;` is not part of the yielded statement. Two consecutive quote characters inside a literal are its escape and re-open the literal, which handles 'it''s' correctly.

Outside a block, a lone `/` line terminates the pending statement if any non-whitespace, non-comment content is pending, and is otherwise discarded. This mirrors EXAplus and is what keeps pre-composite single-statement artifacts valid unchanged.
A `--/` line while a statement is still pending is an error, as is a block that the artifact ends without closing.
Every yielded statement is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace. A statement that strips to empty is not yielded, so stray `;` and blank filler produce nothing.
notes: PREPROC.MODULE_RESOLVER_V1 emits artifact text in VARCHAR(2000000) chunks. The in-database path MUST reassemble every chunk before splitting; the statement_straddling_chunk_boundary case is longer than one chunk and fails loudly for any implementation that splits per chunk.

cases.name: single_block_wrapped_lua_script
cases.description: The canonical shape of every library module published so far: one CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT wrapped in block markers because its Lua body contains semicolons.

cases.name: single_semicolon_terminated_statement
cases.description: A statement with no semicolons in its body needs no block markers; the terminating semicolon is not part of the statement.

cases.name: block_then_semicolon_statement
cases.description: The module/contract scenario: a block-wrapped statement whose body keeps its semicolons, followed by a semicolon-terminated statement. Exactly two statements, no marker lines.

cases.name: semicolon_inside_string_literal
cases.description: A semicolon inside a single-quoted string literal does not terminate the statement.
statements: INSERT INTO PREPROC_RT.SEED_V1 (label) VALUES ('a;b')

cases.name: escaped_quote_inside_string_literal
cases.description: A doubled quote is the literal's escape, so the semicolon after it is still inside the string. Two statements, not three.
cases.text:
INSERT INTO PREPROC_RT.SEED_V1 (label) VALUES ('it''s; fine');
INSERT INTO PREPROC_RT.SEED_V1 (label) VALUES ('next');
statements: INSERT INTO PREPROC_RT.SEED_V1 (label) VALUES ('it''s; fine')
INSERT INTO PREPROC_RT.SEED_V1 (label) VALUES ('next')

cases.name: semicolon_inside_line_comment
cases.description: A semicolon in a `--` comment does not split. The comment precedes the statement and stays part of its text.
cases.text:
-- note; this semicolon must not split the statement
CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.T_V1 (c INT);
statements:
-- note; this semicolon must not split the statement
CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.T_V1 (c INT)

cases.name: semicolon_inside_block_comment
cases.description: A `/* */` comment spans lines and its semicolons do not split.

cases.name: semicolon_inside_quoted_identifier
cases.description: A semicolon inside a double-quoted identifier does not split.
statements: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT."odd;name_V1" (c INT)

cases.name: lone_slash_terminates_unwrapped_statement
cases.description: A statement with no semicolons and no block markers, closed by the EXAplus lone `/`. The `/` is a terminator, never part of the statement.
cases.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t end
/
statements:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t end

cases.name: stray_lone_slash_discarded
cases.description: A lone `/` with nothing pending is discarded rather than yielding an empty statement.
statements: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.T_V1 (c INT)

cases.name: crlf_line_endings
cases.description: A CRLF artifact splits identically to an LF one, and the yielded statement carries LF endings.
cases.text:
--/
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t; end
/
statements:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t; end

cases.name: trailing_whitespace_on_marker_lines
cases.description: Marker lines are recognized ignoring surrounding whitespace, and the statement is stripped.
statements: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.T_V1 (c INT)

cases.name: block_body_keeps_its_trailing_semicolon
cases.description: A block body is preserved verbatim, so an author's trailing semicolon is kept. This is what lets a CREATE FUNCTION whose syntax ends in `END;` round-trip.
statements: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.T_V1 (c INT);

cases.name: comments_between_statements_are_filler
cases.description: Blank lines and whole-line comments outside any statement are inter-statement filler: they are discarded, and a comment immediately before a `--/` does not make the block marker illegal.
cases.text:
-- header comment

--/
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.E_V1 AS
function e(t) return t; end
/

-- trailing note
statements:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.E_V1 AS
function e(t) return t; end

cases.name: two_statements_on_one_line
cases.description: A terminating semicolon ends the statement mid-line; the rest of the line starts the next one.
cases.text: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.A_V1 (c INT); CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.B_V1 (c INT);
statements: CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.A_V1 (c INT)
CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.B_V1 (c INT)

cases.name: no_terminator_at_end_of_file
cases.description: An artifact that ends with neither `;` nor `/` still yields its pending statement. This is the pre-composite single-statement form and MUST stay valid.
cases.text:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t end
statements:
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t end

cases.name: blank_artifact_yields_no_statements
cases.description: Whitespace and comments alone carry no statement.

cases.name: composite_lua_entry_python_udf_and_table
cases.description: A realistic composite artifact: a Lua entry script, a Python UDF companion whose body contains semicolons and a blank line, and a table. Three statements in file order.
statements:
CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.CONFD_JOB_LOG_V1 (
    job_id   DECIMAL(18,0),
    payload  VARCHAR(2000000)
)

cases.name: statement_straddling_chunk_boundary
cases.description: One block-wrapped statement whose Lua body is padded past 2,000,000 characters, so the resolver's first VARCHAR(2000000) chunk ends in the middle of it — inside a string literal at that. An implementation that splits per chunk instead of after reassembly cannot produce this single statement.
text:
--/
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.BIG_V1 AS
function big(sqltext)
    local pad = "

error_cases.name: unterminated_block
error_cases.description: A `--/` block the artifact never closes with a lone `/` line.
error_cases.text:
--/
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t; end

error_cases.name: block_marker_inside_unterminated_statement
error_cases.description: A `--/` opens while a semicolon-terminated statement is still pending, which would silently swallow the pending text.
error_cases.text:
CREATE TABLE PREPROC_RT.A_V1 (c INT)
--/
CREATE OR REPLACE LUA SCRIPT PREPROC_RT.M_V1 AS
function m(t) return t; end
/
